subject: reading
title: The Big Pumpkin
about: Two friends tug a big pumpkin free on a crisp day. Practises short vowels with ck, ch, th, ll and blends (Nick, stuck, crunch, thud, hill, snaps, bumps) and one longer word, pumpkin, plus the tricky words the, a, yellow, down, we, is and what. Decodable at CKLA Unit 1, so he can read it alone.
tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again; ask him what the red and yellow bits are.

passage.text:
Kim and Nick run up the hill.
Red and yellow bits spin down.
Crunch, crunch, crunch!

On top sits a big fat pumpkin.
"Can we get it?" asks Kim.
Kim tugs.
Nick tugs.
The pumpkin is stuck.

Then the stem snaps.
It bumps down the hill.
Thud!
It stops at Mom's van.

Mom grins.
"What a big pumpkin!"

cards.note: Kim and Nick run up the hill at the start.

cards.q: Where do Kim and Nick run?
cards.note: The first line says they run up the hill.

cards.q: What is on top of the hill?
cards.note: On top sits a big fat pumpkin.
It bumps down the hill and stops at Mom's van.
They run up the hill first; the stem snaps later.
At the end Mom grins and says What a big pumpkin!

cards.q: How does Mom feel at the end?
cards.note: Mom grins, so she is glad.

cards.q: Why does the pumpkin bump down the hill?
cards.note: When the stem snaps, the pumpkin comes loose and bumps down the hill.

cards.q: What does snaps mean in the story?
cards.note: When the stem snaps, it breaks with a quick crack.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Pumpkin is in the story; napkin and pumps are look-alikes that are not.
